commits.pr_title: [Core] Offload raw-prompt preprocessing to renderer thread pool in AsyncLLM
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #49317.

`AsyncLLM.add_request()` calls `InputProcessor.process_inputs()` synchronously on the asyncio event loop thread. For raw prompts this includes tokenization and HF multimodal preprocessing (image resize/patchify into `pixel_values`), which holds the event loop for the whole duration. Under concurrent multimodal requests everything serializes before reaching the EngineCore scheduler, so `max_num_batched_tokens` cannot help and the GPU sits nearly idle while a single CPU thread crunches images.

The OpenAI server path does not hit this because the renderer already offloads MM processing to its thread pool (`BaseRenderer._process_multimodal_async`). The gap is direct `AsyncLLM.generate()` callers passing raw prompts, which is common in RL and scoring frameworks.

## Changes

- `InputProcessor` now exposes `process_inputs_async`, built with the existing `make_async` helper on the renderer's existing thread pool, so concurrency stays bounded by `renderer_num_workers` and no new executor is introduced.
- `AsyncLLM.add_request()` awaits the async variant for raw prompts. Already-rendered `EngineInput` dicts keep the direct synchronous call since they skip preprocessing entirely, so the hot serving path is unchanged.

The streaming-input path (`_add_streaming_input_request`) still calls `process_inputs` directly; its per-chunk prompts are typically token ids, so it is left for a follow-up if needed.

## Not a duplicate

Checked open PRs referencing #49317 and searched for related work on async input processing in `AsyncLLM.add_request`; no open PR addresses this issue.

## Test plan

- Added `test_raw_prompt_preprocessing_off_event_loop` to `tests/v1/engine/test_async_llm.py` (text and vision engines): spies on `InputPreprocessor.preprocess` and asserts it runs off the event loop thread. Needs CUDA, will run in CI.
- `pre-commit` (ruff, ruff format, mypy) passes on the changed files.
- Benchmark on an H100 (concurrent multimodal requests via `AsyncLLM.generate()`, baseline vs patched) in progress; numbers follow below in a comment.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Fix dangling temporary in AWQ gemm torch::stable::sum dim arg
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

`awq_gemm` (in `csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/awq/gemm_kernels.cu`) ends with:

```cpp
return torch::stable::sum(_out_feats, 0);
```

The scalar `0` is wrapped into a single-element `HeaderOnlyArrayRef` whose constructor only stores a **pointer** to the temporary. When this `sum` call is **not inlined**, that temporary's stack slot is overwritten (by the adjacent CUDA launch-config setup) before the boxed dispatcher reads it → the serialized `dim` becomes garbage → an out-of-range `aten::sum.dim_IntList` and the engine dies:

```
RuntimeError: torch_call_dispatcher("aten::sum", "dim_IntList", ...) API call failed (csrc/.../stable/ops.h)
→ EngineDeadError
```

## Why it usually doesn't reproduce

Mainstream build toolchains happen to **inline** this call, folding `0` into a register so the dangling pointer is never materialized — both the manylinux gcc-toolset-13 PyPI wheels and the `nvidia/cuda:*-devel-ubuntu22.04` (GCC 10) docker images are safe. The latent bug surfaces when the kernel is compiled by a toolchain that does **not** inline it (reproduced with GCC 11.4): `InternVL2-2B-AWQ` crashes at first decode with the trace above.

## Fix

Pass the reduction dim through a named, lifetime-stable `std::vector<int64_t>` plus an explicit `IntHeaderOnlyArrayRef`, so correctness no longer depends on the compiler choosing to inline `torch::stable::sum`. No behavior change on builds that already inline.

```cpp
std::vector<int64_t> sum_dim = {0};
return torch::stable::sum(
    _out_feats,
    torch::headeronly::IntHeaderOnlyArrayRef(sum_dim.data(), sum_dim.size()));
```

## Test

Built the `awq_gemm` reduction path standalone against the runtime torch with GCC 11.4: the scalar-`0` form fails (`aten::sum dim_IntList API call failed`), while the explicit-`IntHeaderOnlyArrayRef` form returns the correct reduced shape. Functionally equivalent on toolchains that already inline.

commits.pr_title: (feat): optionally disable lookup on PD decode
commits.pr_body:
The original implementation is done by @ivanium .

## Summary
This PR introduces the `enable_lookup` flag for `MooncakeStoreConnector`, to be added in `kv_connector_extra_config` with `kv_consumer` role. This flag is for a PD setup where decode instance doesn't read from or write to the Mooncake, and only contributes its segment for extending prefill worker KV cache capacity. e.g.
```
--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MultiConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail"},{"kv_connector":"MooncakeStoreConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"enable_cross_layers_blocks":false,"enable_lookup":false}}]}}'
```
- This avoid the potential overhead brought by the useless lookup, e.g. DSV4
- This also allows enabling a naive heterogeneous TP Mooncake PD setup for not yet compatible models, e.g. K3

## Test
### Unit

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py
22 passed
```

New `test_disabled_lookup_reports_no_hit_without_querying_client`, 21 are pre-existing.

### End to end

Kimi-K3 1P1D on 6x GB300 nodes / 24 GPUs: prefill TP8 across 2 nodes (prefix caching on,
mamba align mode, `MultiConnector` = Nixl + MooncakeStore), decode DEP16 across 4
nodes (`--no-enable-prefix-caching`, store child as in the Summary above). Mooncake 
 `enable_lookup: false`, `global_segment_size: 100GB` per rank.

With the flag, all 16 decode ranks start and report the mode, once each:

```
[worker.py:1279] Mooncake store in capacity-only mode: segment mounted
(global_segment_size=107374182400), KV transfer disabled.
```

The master shows all 24 ranks joining the pool. Before traffic, then at peak:

```
Mem Storage: 0 B / 2.34 TB (0.0%)      | Keys: 0     | Clients: 24
Mem Storage: 2.11 TB / 2.34 TB (90.0%) | Keys: 90357 | Clients: 24
```

The pool is 24 x ~97.5 GB usable, of which prefill owns only 8 x ~97.5 GB = 0.78 TB, so at
least ~1.3 TB of prefill's offloaded KV is resident in decode-owned segments. Decode itself
issues no put/get.

AA-LCR (100 long-context samples, concurrency 8) was run twice back to back against
the same deployment: once against an empty store, then again with the first run's blocks resident.

| | cold store | warm store |
|---|---|---|
| score (llm_judge) | 0.78 | 0.78 |
| samples / request errors | 100 / **0** | 100 / **0** |
| eval duration | 343.85 s | 307.57 s |
| master `Get` | `Item=0.00` for the whole run | up to 906 items/s |
| prefill external prefix cache hit | 6.7% peak | 44.2% peak |

The score is unchanged, validated as e2e correctness. Note the store was already ~86% full
when the warm run started (evictions 1 -> 3 during it), so some cold-run blocks were dropped
before they could be re-read.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Add cache_salt support to Anthropic Messages API
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Closes #46688.

The OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions / Completions APIs accept a `cache_salt`
for explicit prefix-cache isolation in multi-user deployments. The Anthropic
Messages API (`/v1/messages`) did not expose it, so clients built on the
Anthropic schema had to switch API formats just to get deterministic
prefix-cache isolation.

## Change

- Add `cache_salt: str | None` to `AnthropicMessagesRequest`, with the same
  description as the OpenAI chat field.
- Pass it through `_build_base_request` into the internal
  `ChatCompletionRequest`, which already owns the field and its
  `check_cache_salt_support` validator — so validation and engine behavior
  match the OpenAI routes exactly.

Only the Messages (generation) path is affected; `AnthropicCountTokensRequest`
is untouched (no generation, no prefix-cache isolation concern). Behavior is
unchanged when `cache_salt` is omitted (defaults to `None`).

## Test

`tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py::TestCacheSalt`:
- `cache_salt` on the Anthropic request reaches the converted
  `ChatCompletionRequest`.
- omitting it leaves the field `None` (unchanged default).

Note: I was unable to run the suite locally (no CUDA/torch on my dev machine);
the files pass `py_compile` and the change mirrors the existing
`kv_transfer_params` pass-through — relying on CI to execute the tests.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][MLA] Mask the AITER MLA small-head verify flatten causally
commits.pr_body:
# [ROCm][MLA] Mask the AITER MLA small-head verify flatten causally

## Purpose

On `ROCM_AITER_MLA`, a multi-token speculative verify block with fewer than 16 query
heads per rank is flattened into single-token Gluon decodes with no causality check
(`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py:1006-1009`), and every resulting
row is handed its request's **entire** paged-KV range, `per_req_len[row_req]`
(`rocm_aiter_mla.py:1035`). That range already spans the block being verified, since
`paged_kv_indptr` is the cumsum of `seq_lens` (`rocm_aiter_mla.py:496-502`), so
verify position `t` attends to the draft tokens after it -- the tokens it is supposed
to be checking. This PR gives row `t` a causal window instead, and corrects the
flatten's comments, which claim the committed prefix. Only the sub-16-head Gluon flatten
is affected; `num_heads >= 16` falls through to the correctly masked `mla_decode_fwd`
(`rocm_aiter_mla.py:1100-1111`).

Nothing raises and nothing warns: the output is plausible, just conditioned on tokens
that have not been verified yet, and a target that has already seen the draft tokens
accepts more of them, so the defect presents as a throughput win. This fixes code
merged the same day -- the Gluon decode path, the verify flatten and the widened
head-count check all arrived together in #50000. There is no existing issue to link.

**Blast radius.** At head counts that divide 16 this is a regression: those
configurations previously took the correctly-masked `mla_decode_fwd` path, and
DeepSeek-family models land there -- 128 MLA heads is 8 per rank at TP=16. At
non-divisors such as Kimi-K3's 12 per rank it is newly permitted rather than
regressed, since `is_valid_num_heads` previously rejected them at construction and
those deployments did not start at all. 

**The fix.** Row `r*qlen + t` gets `seq_len_r - (qlen - 1) + t` entries instead of
`seq_len_r`. Each row's causal window is a prefix of that request's slice, since
`paged_kv_indices` lists pages in ascending position order, so no new indexing is
required; rows clamp to zero for cudagraph padding requests. It reduces KV work
rather than adding any. `min_kv_seq_len` moves with it, from `per_req_len.min()` to
the shortest row actually submitted.

## Test Plan

`tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_causal_verify_mask.py` is added in this
PR. On a ROCm host with AITER installed:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 python3 -m pytest -v \
    tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_causal_verify_mask.py
```

It drives the real `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder` and `AiterMLAImpl.forward_mqa` over a
five-request batch that includes a `seq_len 0` cudagraph padding request, and asserts on
the `(page_table, seq_info)` handed to the Gluon kernel that verify row `t` of request
`r` gets exactly `context_r + t + 1` entries as an ascending prefix of that request's
slice. The kernel is spied rather than run, so the gate is ROCm plus AITER.

## Test Result

On unmodified `main`, every row of a fresh 8-token verify block sees the whole block:

```
    min_kv_seq_len passed to the kernel: 8   (verify block length is 8)
      row 0  KV [100, 101, 102, 103, 104, 105, 106, 107]   <-- sees 7 future positions
    ... rows 1-6 identical ...
      row 7  KV [100, 101, 102, 103, 104, 105, 106, 107]
  [FAIL] row lengths are 1..8 (strictly causal)  got [8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8]
```

this fix:

```
    min_kv_seq_len passed to the kernel: 1   (verify block length is 8)
      row 0  KV [100]
    ... rows 1-6 grow by one ...
      row 7  KV [100, 101, 102, 103, 104, 105, 106, 107]
  [PASS] row lengths are 1..8 (strictly causal)  got [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]
```

The output was also compared against float32 causal and full-range references over nine
batch shapes, after calibrating that reference against the kernel on ordinary decode
rows. On unmodified `main` it matches the full-range reference at the calibrated noise
floor while diverging from the causal one by close to 1.0 relative on short contexts --
on fresh requests with zero context, `9.94e-01` causal against `3.59e-03` full-range.
With this fix that reverses: `2.75e-03` causal, `2.44e+00` full-range.

Limitations:

* The comparisons are at the tensor level, against float32 references recomputed from
  the same inputs: they establish which KV window the kernel was given, not end-to-end
  quality, which is not claimed.
* The divisor-count regression, and the claim that `num_heads >= 16` is unaffected, are
  argued from reading the source rather than from executing it; both arms ran at 12
  heads.
* `main` and the runtime are not the same build: the module under test is `main`
  byte-for-byte, but the torch/AITER/vLLM runtime around it comes from a published
  ROCm image, for the reason given at the start of this section.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][CI] Prevent common ops imports from initializing CUDA
commits.pr_body:
The [PyTorch Fullgraph job](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/81692/summary?jid=019fb955-8175-4d2d-ac07-a66e527c95b1&tab=output) started failing with `Cannot re-initialize CUDA in forked subprocess`, while the [Extra Initialization job](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/81692/summary?jid=019fb955-8143-4e3d-84b2-1ce20e29275e&tab=output) failed when the Kimi initialization test unexpectedly ran a model profile. I ran `git bisect` between the failing commit `fe33a3ed` and the known-good commit `5d7647a1`. It identified `92643d68` from [#50242](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50242) as the first bad commit. That commit added a package-level re-export which made a lightweight common-op import pull in model/config dependencies and initialize CUDA before EngineCore process creation. So this is one import-time regression behind both failures, not a Kimi runtime bug.

- Remove the eager `fused_allreduce_rms_norm` re-export from the common-ops package.
- Import the fused helper directly in the three model files that use it.
- Run `can_initialize`'s EngineCore in-process so its KV-cache patch is retained even if a later import forces spawn.

commits.pr_title: [Rust][Benchmark] Prevent invalid token IDs in random benchmarks
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

  Random benchmark generation treated every ID in `0..vocab_size` as valid for
  built-in tiktoken encodings. That assumption is incorrect for sparse
  vocabularies:

  - `o200k_base` contains 275 unassigned IDs in the configured range.
  - `cl100k_base` contains 16 unassigned IDs in the configured range.

  When the random dataset sampled one of these IDs, decoding panicked. Release
  builds use abort-on-panic behavior, so the entire benchmark process terminated.
  With the default input length and 1,000 prompts, encountering an invalid ID was
  effectively certain.

  Build the allowed-token pool from the contiguous decodable token range plus
  the registered special token IDs. This removes unassigned IDs while preserving
  valid special tokens and the existing behavior of dense built-in encodings.

commits.pr_title: Enable ModelOpt FP8 emulation on SM80
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

ModelOpt FP8 checkpoints are currently rejected on NVIDIA A100 GPUs before vLLM can select its existing weight-only FP8 execution path:

```text
ValueError: The quantization method modelopt is not supported for the current GPU. Minimum capability: 89. Current capability: 80.
```

This PR lowers `ModelOptFp8Config`'s minimum CUDA capability from SM89 to SM80. On GPUs with capability SM80 through SM88, it also emits one model-level warning explaining that FP8 is not executed natively, that vLLM will use emulation for the model, and that some models may run more slowly. SM89 and newer GPUs retain their existing behavior and do not receive the warning.

This enables a serialized ModelOpt `quant_algo=FP8` checkpoint to load on A100 without a backend override. The exercised model was `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-FP8`. While it may appear counter-intuitive, the emulated FP8 actually shows better performance than the unquantized BF16 model due to the bandwidth reduction achieved for bandwidth-limited GEMMs. (Added a warning because for dense/compute-limited GEMM models, FP8 emulation may lag native bf16 execution due to the dequantization overhead.)

## Test Plan

The before/after reproduction uses one NVIDIA A100 80GB GPU, tensor parallelism 1, vLLM 0.26.0, BF16 activations, and an FP8 KV cache. The tested FP8 checkpoint revision was `f8dc1c0afee92f44417695b4f5ddca9afc95ea58`.

Run this command with stock vLLM 0.26.0, then run the same command after applying this PR:

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-FP8 \
  --revision f8dc1c0afee92f44417695b4f5ddca9afc95ea58 \
  --served-model-name nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-FP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-num-seqs 512 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 25088 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000
```

Stock vLLM 0.26.0 exits at the capability check shown above. With this PR applied to the same vLLM version, the checkpoint loads, the server becomes ready, and the existing automatic FP8 fallback is selected for both dense and MoE layers. No backend-selection environment variable or command-line override is used.

For the matched BF16 control, start a second run on the same A100 with:

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16 \
  --revision 2d59de1cbd51c0adf384eb906b766d1aee0e0517 \
  --served-model-name nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-num-seqs 512 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 27136 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000
```

The two servers use the same GPU, vLLM version, TP size, KV-cache dtype, maximum sequence count, memory utilization, block size, and prefix-cache setting. Their `max-model-len` values differ because each was set to the exercised capacity for that weight format; the GSM8K prompts and generation settings are identical.

The GSM8K evaluator used for the reported results is public at `NVIDIA/srt-slurm`, commit `cb651682117df129162cd276cf567ec70dc57b36`. Clone that revision:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/srt-slurm.git
cd srt-slurm
git checkout cb651682117df129162cd276cf567ec70dc57b36
```

With the FP8 server running, execute:

```bash
python3 src/srtctl/benchmarks/scripts/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py \
  --host http://localhost \
  --port 8000 \
  --model nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-FP8 \
  --num-questions 1319 \
  --max-tokens 16000 \
  --num-shots 8 \
  --temperature 0.6 \
  --seed 42 \
  --save-results ./gsm8k-fp8.json
```

With the BF16 control server running, execute:

```bash
python3 src/srtctl/benchmarks/scripts/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py \
  --host http://localhost \
  --port 8000 \
  --model nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16 \
  --num-questions 1319 \
  --max-tokens 16000 \
  --num-shots 8 \
  --temperature 0.6 \
  --seed 42 \
  --save-results ./gsm8k-bf16.json
```

## Test Result

The stock FP8 run failed before model loading with the SM89 minimum-capability error. Applying this PR changed the same command to a successful load and healthy server. The full FP8 GSM8K run and the BF16 control both completed all 1,319 questions with no request failures.

| Metric | BF16 weights | ModelOpt FP8 weights | FP8 delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Completed questions | 1,319 / 1,319 | 1,319 / 1,319 | — |
| Accuracy | 61.1069% | 58.3776% | -2.7293 pp |
| Invalid responses | 0% | 0% | — |
| Evaluation wall time | 539.667 s | 435.493 s | -19.30% |
| Questions/s | 2.4441 | 3.0288 | +23.92% |
| Total output tokens | 588,906 | 611,214 | +22,308 |
| Output tokens/s | 1,091.24 | 1,403.50 | +28.62% |
| Full job wall time | 13:31 | 11:56 | -11.71% |
| Process exit status | 0 | 0 | — |

The FP8 run was approximately 1.24x faster by evaluation time and 1.29x faster by output-token throughput, with a 2.73 percentage-point accuracy reduction in this single full-dataset run. Because the FP8 run generated more output tokens than the BF16 control, output tokens per second is the more useful normalized throughput comparison than total job wall time. These results establish the measured performance/accuracy tradeoff rather than claiming that every model or workload will speed up.

commits.pr_title: [graceful shutdown] fix http server start firstly before app signal handler register
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
For now, `server.serve` is run concurrently with the app signal SIGINT and SIGTERM handlers. There is a race condition.
1. `server.serve` will first call `capture_signals`. `capture_signals` will overwrite the signal SIGINT and SIGTERM handler before invoke `server._serve` which will chain invoke `server.startup` and start the server

If the coroutine `server.serve` is delayed after app signal SIGINT and SIGTERM handlers being registered, the app signal handlers will be overwrite in `server.capture_signals`.  This will shutdown the server firstly, the app graceful shutdown procedure will not work as expected.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][ViT] Detect Triton-AMD kernels at their new aiter location
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`flash_attn_triton_available()` in `vllm/platforms/rocm.py` gates whether `AttentionBackendEnum.FLASH_ATTN` is offered for the ViT encoder on ROCm. The check looks for `flash_attn.flash_attn_triton_amd`, but ROCm/flash-attention commit [`3f94643`](https://github.com/ROCm/flash-attention/commit/3f94643) (2026-03-12, *\"[AMD] Migrate to Triton Backend to Aiter\"*) removed that subpackage and moved the kernels into aiter at `aiter.ops.triton._triton_kernels.flash_attn_triton_amd`.

After that migration, `find_spec(\"flash_attn.flash_attn_triton_amd\")` returns `None` on every current ROCm wheel, so the ViT silently falls back to `TORCH_SDPA`. On gfx1151 (Strix Halo / RDNA3.5) the SDPA path produces NaN/Inf image embeddings and the LM collapses into an endless `!` stream. Other ROCm targets just lose the fast path.

This PR widens the detection to accept either the legacy subpackage or the new aiter location, restoring Triton-AMD as an available ViT backend wherever the kernels actually live.

## Changes

`vllm/platforms/rocm.py` — `flash_attn_triton_available()`: return `False` only when **both** import paths are missing.

No behavior change when `flash_attn.flash_attn_triton_amd` still exists (older builds). When only the aiter path exists (current builds), the function now correctly returns `True`.

## Test Plan / Result

- Static: verified the new check returns `True` against an aiter build where only the new path exists, and `False` when neither path exists.
- On gfx1151, using the explicit `--mm-encoder-attn-backend TRITON_ATTN` flag (a different code path — vLLM's own `vit_triton_attn_wrapper`) I confirmed the Triton ViT kernels produce correct image embeddings on Qwen3-VL-A3B AWQ.

**Shortcoming I want to be transparent about:** I have *not* been able to end-to-end verify the auto-selected `AttentionBackendEnum.FLASH_ATTN` ViT path that this PR enables. In the environment I tested, aiter's JIT-built `.so`s are not discoverable by `importlib` due to a separate packaging issue, so the flash_attn → aiter call chain can't currently run to completion here. The detection logic in this PR is the narrow, obviously-correct half of the fix; the packaging issue is being tracked/fixed separately.

Reviewers with a working aiter install can validate the full path by unsetting `--mm-encoder-attn-backend` and confirming ViT selects `FLASH_ATTN` and produces correct embeddings.

Signed-off-by: Adrian Kurt <info@zzit.ch>

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Quark][7/N] Use MXFP4 linear kernel abstraction for `emulation` backend
commits.pr_body:
Co-authored-by: Claude

## Purpose

Refactor `QuarkOCP_MX` (the Quark OCP MX4/MX6 linear scheme) to use the shared `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear` kernel abstraction for its `emulation` backend, similar to the refactor done in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49348 for the `aiter` backend.

Previously `QuarkOCP_MX` hard-coded its own `self.emulate` boolean and directly registered/dispatched the AITER `gemm_with_dynamic_quant` custom op inline, duplicating logic that the kernel-selection framework already provides for other quantization schemes (FP8, NVFP4, MXFP8, ...).

This introduces `EmulationMxfp4LinearKernel` as a proper `MxFp4LinearKernel` implementation selected through `init_mxfp4_linear_kernel`, as well as `EmulationMxfp6LinearKernel` to avoid mixing up mxfp4/mxfp6 oracles.

Additionally, this PR extends the mxfp4 kernel config with `activation_quant_key` so kernel dispatch is done according to supported `QuantKey`.

**This is a pure refactor PR. No new hardware backend or numerical behavior is introduced.** Motivation is to standardize mxfp4 linear backends throughout vLLM codebase, and avoid `quark_ocp_mx.py`-specific code/dispatch that can benefit all checkpoint producers (compressed-tensors, etc.). e.g. helpful for https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46676

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Restore Mistral tool-parser compatibility after unification
commits.pr_body:
- `git bisect` identified [`1a20d23dab6e`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/1a20d23dab6eef0ce6ab97b7e03c944683cdf90b), [vLLM #48947](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48947), as the first revision with this failure.
- The unified parser moved `bot_token` and `bot_token_id` onto its nested engine and made legacy extraction assume a request object, breaking two behaviors preserved by the former `MistralToolParser`.

Motivation:

- [AMD CI build 11504 — Language Models Test (Extended Generation)](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/11504/list?sid=019fb494-a023-4562-bbca-b7c0d94c5c99&tab=output)

PR #48947 replaced the former standalone `MistralToolParser` with an adapter over the unified Mistral parser engine. `bot_token` and `bot_token_id` remained available only on the nested engine, while existing callers still access them on the adapter. Restoring those properties exposed a second compatibility regression: `_legacy_extract_tool_calls` directly accessed `request.tool_choice` and `request.tools`, although the established parser API permits `request=None` and the former implementation tolerated it.
